TcpStack tests: every stack is disposed (32 ran their FIN retransmissions and timers to the end of the run), ServerWrite collects behind a lock and no longer sleeps, EchoTest waits on conditions, DataPacketWithoutPsh asserts before the sweep could flush the ACK for it, the ring-wrap test wraps a 1300-byte ring and reads a retransmission back across its end; 4 new tests - ListenAny with the client's endpoints, the SYN's MSS and window scale honored, a SYN on an established tuple draws one challenge ACK, sequence numbers crossing 2^32 inside a segment with a retransmission from before the wrap, which found a stack bug: a segment starting exactly half the sequence space ahead negated to an overflowing overlap and threw per segment, it counts as ahead now (Opus max review taken)

TcpStack: the conventions - the listener's accept methods and the connection's send take a required cancellation token; the stream links the caller's token inside the try, so a dispose that races a read ends the stream instead of throwing, and awaits with Vhc(); the null-forgiving operators are gone (the retransmit ring throws if read while unallocated, the test context is required); the fast retransmit guards its own send; the stack's uncalled StopListening(IPEndPoint) overload is removed (Opus max and Sol reviews taken)

TcpStack: the connection count is one number - the diagnostics' atomic (AddConnections, which keeps the peak), taken before a connection enters the table and given back on every path out of it (a lost race for the 4-tuple, a failed SYN-ACK, a close), where the stack kept a second count beside it; every removal from the table is by key and value, so a late close cannot remove a successor on the same 4-tuple; a disposed or closed connection refuses a late MarkEstablished and Close, so its client never reaches the accept queue and nothing is counted twice; 1 regression test (Opus max and Sol reviews taken)

TcpStack: the texts say what the code does - ITcpStack's summary (no LwipTcpStack), the README's limits (no out-of-order reassembly and no SACK, no TIME_WAIT), the options' remarks (the buffer defaults are the values Android throughput was tuned against, the timing defaults follow RFC 6298), the comments that explained the code by code that no longer exists, the integration test's sizes, and TestDocumentation.md, which describes the two WinDivert tests and their run on a Windows VM (Opus max review taken)

TcpStack: the idle timeout is one sweep of the stack - a timer at IdleCheckInterval over every connection (PollIdle), parked while no connection exists - where each connection ran a task and a timer of its own for its whole life; IdleCheckInterval must be between 1 ms and 49 days; the test assembly raises the thread pool's minimum, since MSTest's non-cooperative timeouts park two pool threads per running test and under memory load the pool stopped growing, which stalled whole runs and failed unrelated tests; 1 regression test (Opus max and Sol reviews taken)

TcpStack: the per-packet costs that bought nothing go - the unread pipe count is a plain field under the lock every writer already holds, where each access paid an atomic; the stack-wide pipe total is summed when the diagnostics read it, every 5 s, where every segment paid a stack-wide atomic; the eleven-argument ACK trace and the retransmit counter run under VerboseLogging only; the maintenance interest is taken by the send and receive paths and given back by the sweep alone, where every other upload segment flipped the stack's timer (a Timer.Change each); the timestamp is taken once per segment; 80 MB through 40 connections takes about 70 ms where it took 211 to 265 ms, the peak memory unchanged; 1 regression test (Opus max and Sol reviews taken)

TcpStack: a segment on an established connection is processed, carries the peer's window and counts as its activity only when its sequence number is inside the receive window and its ack within [SndUna, SndNxt] (RFC 9293 3.10.7.4; a keepalive one below RcvNxt counts too), an ack of data never sent draws a challenge ACK and nothing else (RFC 5961 5.2), and a segment without the ACK bit is dropped with its data, where any packet naming the 4-tuple could set the peer's window to zero and freeze the sender, or keep an idle connection alive; 4 regression tests (Opus max and Sol reviews taken)
TcpStack: RetxBufferSize is RetransmitBufferSize, named like RetransmitTimeout beside it (a mechanical rename)
DEPR: complex min, max, idxmin, idxmax, cummin, cummax (GH#43770) (#70928)

TcpStack: the handshake's final ACK is accepted with its sequence number anywhere up to the window's edge (RFC 9293 3.10.7.4, the edge as Linux takes it), where only an exact RCV.NXT passed and a lost final ACK followed by a lost first segment left the stack answering every later segment with a SYN-ACK and the peer with a challenge ACK until the peer's RTO; a segment that acknowledges the SYN-ACK but sits outside the window draws a plain ACK, not another SYN-ACK; 3 regression tests (Opus max and Sol reviews taken)
